metadata.note: deep-explainer, fresh technical build (not sourced from ai1-cli or any single document) covering the 8 required points: test case structure, judge prompts, output parsing, bias mitigation, metric abstraction, batch evaluation runner, aggregation, CI/CD integration. 4 acts, 2 points/act. Content is general, well-established LLM-evaluation engineering practice; the one specific citation (position/verbosity/self-enhancement bias) is Zheng et al. 2023, 'Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena' -- see FACTCHECK.md for the honesty/sourcing method note. No Manim on this machine (pangocairo not installed) -- MANIM lane absorbed into REMOTION, as in the prior two deep-explainer builds. VOX quota: 6 real Wikimedia Commons photographs (public domain / CC0 / CC BY), used as METAPHOR imagery (filing records, a courtroom, a telegraph operator, scales of justice, two WWII aircraft-assembly-line photos) since the topic itself has no historical referent -- captioned as illustrative, never claimed to depict LLM evaluation literally. This is the 16:9 master; a 9:16 Short is derived via runtime/scripts/shorts.py into short/. Both compiled at 4K (16:9: 3840x2160; 9:16: 2160x3840). GATE P: PENDING, see PEDAGOGY.md.

beats.narration_text: Merhaba — this is Liam, in for Bear. Ask five different eval frameworks how they use an LLM as a judge, and you get five different half-built systems — until you look at what they all actually need underneath: eight real components, from the test case to the CI gate. Let's build the whole pipeline, in order.

show.event: composer cold-opens, spark + 'Merhaba, Liam' greeting settles
command types itself in: the eight-components question
send arms, runningText plays
RESULT lines land in sequence

props.command: Walk me through everything a real LLM-as-a-judge evaluation system needs, in order, from the test case to the CI gate.
output: a test case is a structured object, not a chat
the judge's own answer needs bias-checking, not just parsing
the last mile is a CI gate, not a spreadsheet

beats.narration_text: Every judgment starts with a record, not a conversation. A test case is a structured object: the input prompt, the candidate output being graded, an optional reference answer, and metadata — category, difficulty, the tags a later report will group by.

shot.prompt: real archival photo of index-card / filing-folder records -- illustrative of a structured record, not a literal depiction of LLM evaluation. Already sourced, see media/A1-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow push into the filing folders
serif label lands: 'a record, not a conversation'

beats.narration_text: One fork happens before any of that: is there a reference answer? Reference-based judging compares the candidate against a known-good answer — narrower, more reliable. Reference-free judging asks the judge to grade on the rubric alone, when no gold answer exists.

show.event: question card settles: 'is there a reference answer?'
two outcome cards land: reference-based / reference-free

branches.label: Reference-free
branches.fix: necessary when no gold answer exists

resolver.label: Both are legal
resolver.detail: the fork decides HOW the rubric gets applied

beats.narration_text: Two ways to extract the score. Regex over free text — fast to write, and it silently breaks the moment the judge phrases things differently. Constrained output — JSON mode, or a function-call schema — forces the shape at generation time, so parsing becomes a formality.

show.event: two tracks diverge: regex arcs up warn, constrained output arcs down good

beats.narration_text: Position bias has a direct fix: run the comparison twice, swapping which answer appears first, and keep only the verdicts that agree both times. Disagreement isn't noise to average away — it's the judge admitting the two answers were closer than the rubric could resolve.

show.event: question card: 'does the order change the verdict?'
two outcomes: agrees both ways / disagrees

data.question: Swap the order — does the verdict change?

branches.label: Disagrees
branches.detail: the answers were closer than the rubric resolved

resolver.label: Run it twice, swapped
resolver.detail: the cheapest bias check that exists

beats.narration_text: One more runner habit that pays for itself immediately: cache the judge's verdict on an identical input. Re-run the same candidate against the same rubric, and a cache hit means zero cost and a guaranteed identical score — not a second roll of an inherently noisy dice.

show.event: two tracks: re-run arcs up warn, cache hit arcs down good

tracks.label: Re-run the judge
tracks.outcome: full cost, and a noisy re-roll

beats.narration_text: A batch of individual verdicts isn't a result yet. Someone has to roll thousands of per-case scores into the handful of numbers a team can actually act on — and then decide what those numbers are allowed to block.

shot.prompt: real archival WWII aircraft-production-line photo -- illustrative of continuous production, not a literal depiction. Already sourced, see media/A4-1.source.txt

show.event: treated plate; slow drift down the production line
serif label lands: 'a handful of numbers, not a pile'

beats.narration_text: Wire that comparison into the build, and the evaluation suite stops being a report nobody reads and starts being a gate. Above the threshold, the build passes. Below it, the build fails — the same way a broken unit test already would.

show.event: question card: 'above or below the threshold?'
two outcomes: build passes / build fails

data.question: Is the aggregate above the threshold?

branches.label: Below threshold
branches.fix: build fails, like a broken unit test

resolver.label: The suite is a gate now

beats.narration_text: Your turn — here's the prompt, read it with me. 'Design a minimal LLM-as-a-judge harness for one thing I actually ship: name the test case schema, the judge prompt's four required parts, how you'll mitigate position bias specifically, and the one metric your CI pipeline should gate on first.' That last clause matters — pick ONE metric to gate on before you build ten. Run it. Liam, in for Bear.

show.event: composer cold to 'Your turn.' greeting
the suggested prompt types itself in, word by word
runningText 'paste this into Claude…' settles
